To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
erythrocyte Na economy, Na-Li counter transport and Li leak are modified by different storage conditions.
the Na-Li counter-transport activity of human erythrocytes is elevated in hypertensive subjects and is increased during the storage of cells in plasma.
plasma-stored erythrocytes exhibit increased Na-Li counter-transport and Li leak as compared with KCl solution-storied cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of storage conditions of erythrocytes and their possible influences on the Na-Li counter-transport in human erythrocytes.
the effect of storage on the erythrocyte Na pump and leak.
the effects of different storage conditions in plasma or isotonic KCl on erythrocyte Na economy and Na transport in hypertensive and normotensive subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plasma storage of erythrocytes is not recommended for transport studies.
plasma storage of erythrocytes should be avoided in studies of Na-Li transport.
plasma storage of erythrocytes for 20 hr results in a significant alteration in Na-Li transport parameters and cellular Na concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the erythrocytes should be stored in isotonic KCl solutions for transport studies.
erythrocytes stored in plasma are not a suitable material for transport studies and that isotonic KCl is a suitable preservation media for erythocytes in transport studies.
erythrocyte Na economy and Na transport properties can be modified by the plasma components.

the storage conditions of erythrocytes can have significant effects on the transport measurements.
